title: A small coproduct is the filtered colimit of its finite subcoproducts
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category [def-weil-size-convention] with finite coproducts and all colimits indexed by finite subsets of a small set $J$. For a family $(X_j)_{j\in J}$ for which the coproduct exists, the canonical cocone from the coproducts of the finite subfamilies, indexed by the inclusion-ordered finite subsets of $J$, is a colimit cocone. In particular, in commutative $k$-algebras the coproduct [lem-weil-pbc-commutative-algebras-colimits-exist] $\bigotimes_{j\in J,k}L_j$ is the filtered colimit of the finite tensor coproducts $\bigotimes_{j\in S,k}L_j$.
